title: HIDA: A Hierarchical Dataflow Compiler for High-Level Synthesis
problem: Existing high-level synthesis tools require developers to manually explore the vast dataflow design space, leading to suboptimal designs that scale poorly. Automated exploration of this space is needed to handle increasingly complex HLS applications.
motivation: Automated dataflow optimization in HLS can unlock significant performance improvements while eliminating manual design space exploration, enabling practical synthesis of large-scale hardware accelerators.
method: HIDA introduces hierarchical dataflow representations to model complex dataflow structures and an automated multi-level optimizer that decomposes the optimization problem based on inherent dataflow hierarchy. The framework systematically converts algorithmic descriptions into optimized dataflow implementations on FPGAs, with evaluation using PyTorch neural network models.
key_novelty: Hierarchical decomposition of dataflow optimization that exploits inherent structure to enable scalable automated design space exploration.
contributions: Efficient and versatile hierarchical dataflow representations for modeling complex dataflow structures
Automated multi-level optimizer that decomposes optimization across hierarchy levels
Achieves 8.54× throughput improvement over SOTA HLS tools and 1.29× over SOTA RTL-based accelerators
